content:
Product liability insurance is assessed in connection with harm alleged by other people after using a product, under a specific contract. It is not the same as a commercial warranty, replacing a defective item or withdrawing a batch from shops. For a Moldovan company, preparation starts with products, the company's role and sales markets, not a general promise that every problem is insured.

This article helps manufacturers, importers and distributors organise risk discussion. It does not confirm a policy for every product or activity, determine liability or replace legal, technical or safety assessment. Applicable obligations and possible insurance must be considered separately. The broker explains and intermediates available options; the insurer decides risk acceptance and claims under the contract.

Three different questions: the product, harm and withdrawal

An item can need repair without harming anyone else's property. In another case, a customer may allege damage to another item or a health problem. Separately, the company may incur identification, transport and storage costs for withdrawn products. Record these categories distinctly. One label for every cost can lead to incomplete questions for the insurer.

Do not assume warehouse property insurance also responds after sale. Nor does product liability automatically pay to replace every unit in a batch. Ask how documents relate and which limits apply. Confirmations must refer to the described situation, not merely a product name in a catalogue.

What is the company's role in the sales chain?

Describe manufacturing, importing, repackaging, own-brand labelling, distribution or retail. Explain who sets specifications and checks incoming batches. A distributor changing packaging or instructions must disclose this rather than describing itself only as a commercial intermediary. This helps risk assessment without independently determining legal obligations.

Prepare relevant supplier and customer contracts, including quality, complaint and return provisions. In a group, identify selling and manufacturing entities. Do not assume a policy for one includes them all. Confirm the complete entity names, activities and actual roles being assessed.

Build a useful product list

Group goods by use and relevant characteristics. Identify components, models and variations affecting use. A broad range can be summarised by category, intended purpose, main materials and sales countries. Do not replace descriptions with unexplained codes the assessor cannot interpret.

Include products no longer manufactured but potentially still in use. Disclose new ranges before assuming earlier assessment applies. Retain test, modification and accompanying-document records. An offer based on last year's range does not automatically establish conditions for a product with different composition or use.

Who uses the product and under which conditions?

Describe intended users and settings: homes, workshops, restaurants, construction sites or other premises. State whether the product reaches the final consumer or forms part of another company's product. A component in an assembly can raise different questions from the same component sold separately. Its selling price alone does not determine contractual treatment.

Gather the instructions and warnings actually distributed. Explain what information the buyer receives and how changes are managed. This article does not certify technical documents or advise improvising instructions. Product safety and conformity must be assessed by competent people and procedures for that category.

Batches and deliveries must be traceable

Prepare an example linking the product to supplier, receipt, stock and delivery. Identification may use a batch, serial number or another company reference. Describe limitations honestly: if some units cannot be separated, do not claim immediate identification. Accurate descriptions support useful assessment.

Check whether staff can find a batch's invoices without searching personal accounts. Retain only necessary data and control customer-information access. Commercial records help organise the file but do not confirm cover. Ask which documents the insurer requires and how to transmit them appropriately in a particular situation.

Declare Moldova and foreign sales separately

Record sales countries, proportions and channels: direct sales, traders, online platforms or partners. A shipment from Moldova is not necessarily an exclusively local exposure. Check relevant territory and jurisdiction in the proposal. An export provision cannot be understood only by translating the policy name.

For a foreign customer's requirements, provide exact wording and discuss implications with a legal specialist. This article does not apply other countries' laws to Moldovan businesses or provide export compliance instructions. Check any insurance solution against your products, markets and contracts. Do not promise that every partner requirement is satisfied before comparing documents.

Which scenarios should you prepare?

Describe plausible business situations without calling them already accepted risks. A component might damage an assembly, or a buyer might claim extra costs. Separate observations, assumptions and missing records. Do not attribute the cause to a person or batch before verification.

For each scenario, ask which contractual definition matters, what costs may be assessed and which points remain unconfirmed. Clear questions are more useful than complete-cover language. Keep mismatches between your need and the proposal visible. An absent condition does not become included because it is omitted from the comparison.

Limits, deductible and the company's own costs

The insurance premium is the amount paid for insurance. The deductible is the insured's share of a loss under the contract. Ask about event and period limits and any cost sublimits. Where documents contain such a rule, check how requests connected to one product or batch are grouped.

Ask separately about defence, expertise, transport, replacement, withdrawal and commercial losses. This does not state that these costs are included. It avoids comparing premiums without understanding what remains with the company. Do not borrow other insurance rates or turn a preliminary estimate into a guaranteed price for all manufacturers.

Keep complaints and records in a timeline

When a complaint arrives, record receipt and the original description rather than replacing it with your own conclusion. Keep product identifiers, delivery records and relevant material. Follow competent safety procedures and check policy notification separately. Do not delay urgent protective action to obtain an editorial opinion about the policy.

Assign responsibility for technical review, communication and the insurance file. Do not promise payment on the insurer's behalf. Liability findings and dispute negotiations require legal support. Do not publish a complainant's personal details or upload medical records to a general sales form. Share sensitive information only when necessary through the agreed channel.

Illustrative example: a furniture-component supplier

A distributor receives a report of an assembly failure. It identifies the model, delivery and technical records, separating the component's cost from alleged damage to other property. This is not a real client case and establishes neither the cause, company liability nor acceptance of any expense by an insurer.

The responsible person compares the delivered configuration with records and requests technical review. Staff check whether one unit or other deliveries need investigation. Provide facts and documents for insurance, not only the customer's requested amount. Remediation, safety measures and policy assessment are coordinated but not treated as one document with a guaranteed outcome.

Update assessment when products or suppliers change

Record changes in materials, components, packaging or instructions before treating a product as identical to the previous version. Keep links between versions and delivered batches. If distribution expands into installation, describe the new service. The same trade name does not necessarily mean the same assessed activity.

At renewal, review products and markets with operational staff, not finance alone. Record changed information and clarify document requirements. Do not confirm extended protection to partners until conditions have been checked. Retain the submitted description so responses can be tied to the same products and operations.

Keep an answer attached to the correct product version

When a component, instruction or packaging changes, retain the earlier description alongside the new one. Record which version was submitted for review and which version a written response addresses. An answer about one model or market should not be presented as confirmation for the entire range. This practical record supports a clearer discussion; it neither establishes product compliance nor extends an insurance contract. Where the scope remains unanswered, mark it as unconfirmed.

Frequently asked questions about product liability

Does a warranty replace liability insurance?

Do not treat them as equivalent. Read obligations for the sold product and policy situations separately. Repairing your own goods and third-party harm require different questions.

Can a distributor's activity be considered?

Describe the role, products and actual operations, then check available possibilities. This article does not establish every distributor's eligibility. Disclose importing, repackaging and own-brand sales.

Is withdrawing a batch automatically included?

Do not assume this. Ask separately about withdrawal or recall costs and alleged harm. Availability and conditions must be confirmed in documents.

What should I send initially?

A product description, company role, sales countries and main questions. Then request the assessment list. Do not initially send customer databases, personal data or unrequested sensitive files.
